title: Advance a sheath over a guidewire on a training phantom without losing the wire
instruction: On this training phantom, slide the blue sheath along the wire until it seats against the port, then draw the wire out through the sheath. Let go of everything at the end.
context: Nurse anesthetists "Insert peripheral or central intravenous catheters" (O*NET 29-1151.00). In the Seldinger technique "A sheath or blunt cannula can now be passed over the guidewire into the cavity or vessel" and "After passing a sheath or tube, the guidewire is withdrawn"; "Loss of the guidewire into the cavity or blood vessel is a significant and generally preventable complication" (Wikipedia, Seldinger technique). Here the sheath's valve drags the wire along unless it is held.
setup: Station table; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left). All parts lie on one line at heading 70 deg through the port P (33, 14). Phantom: skin-coloured printed block 20 x 6 x 3 cm, from P to (39.8, 32.8), 9 x 9 mm bore on a 1.5 mm floor; dark grey collar 4 mm proud of its face, 3.6 cm wide, 2.2 cm tall. Wire: black 6 mm cord, 48 cm, 20 g, tip 8 cm inside the bore at (35.7, 21.5), tail at (19.3, -23.6); a white 2 cm band starts at the collar. Sheath: free blue printed sleeve 16 cm long, 14 x 12 mm outside, 9 x 7 mm bore, 25 g, with a raised grip collar (32 mm wide, 20 mm tall, 8 mm thick) 2 cm behind its nose, around the wire from its nose at (24.1, -10.4) to its rear at (18.6, -25.5); the rear 6 cm is a 2.75 cm tall hub caging a free 10 g valve pad (20 x 8 x 10 mm) that rests on the wire. The tail ends 2 cm inside the rear.
scoring: Score 0 if: before the sheath is first seated, the white band moves more than 1.5 cm from its start at any time (latched for the trial); a gripper is within 3.5 cm of the wire or sheath at the end; the sheath lies more than 1 cm off the port line; its nose advanced less than 12 cm; in a real trial, the phantom is moved. Otherwise: 0.3 nose advanced 12 cm or more, not seated; 0.6 seated (nose within 5 mm of the collar), wire tip not 3 cm out past the sheath's rear; 1.0 seated and the wire tip at least 3 cm out past the rear, at rest 1 s.
reset_notes: Thread the wire back through the sheath from its rear, push its tip 8 cm into the bore so the band sits at the collar, and slide the sheath back until its nose is 26 cm from the port and the tail is 2 cm inside the hub.
fidelity: Scaled model: a 6 mm cord stands in for a sub-millimetre guidewire, a sleeve without dilator for the sheath. Wire: rigid 2 cm segments with bending springs, no twist; friction 0.5. The hub valve is a free weighted pad on the wire (real kit: silicone O-ring); its drag beats the wire's table friction, so an unheld wire moves with the sheath. The raised grip collar near the nose is a test-rig feature for the robot gripper (real sheaths are pushed at the hub). Phantom rigid, no tissue.
